prices.q: Why are there no prices on the site?
prices.a: Tools give you scope and timeline, not a number. Pricing is set in a short call, matched to your actual work.

time.a: Work ships in phases. The first usable phase reaches you well before the full build and runs from day one.

ownership.q: Who owns the code and access?
ownership.a: You do — source, domain, hosting, and every key. Nothing stays locked to us.

iran.q: Does it run reliably from Iran?
iran.a: Yes. Infrastructure, fonts, and tools are chosen to stay fast and reachable from Iran.

assistant.a: Yes — soon you'll talk to it directly on the assistant page and see for yourself.

Roi.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own inputs, not a sales guarantee.

full.title: Lost-sales calculator
full.intro: See what manual replies cost, using your own numbers. The result updates live and the link is shareable.
full.methodBody: Lost sales = unanswered messages × sale conversion rate × average order value.
assumptions: Unanswered messages = total messages × (1 minus the answered share).
Freed hours assume an average of 3 minutes per message.
These figures are estimates and don't replace your real business data.

Terms.title: The framework, before we start
Terms.banner: This page is a framework, not a contract; each project gets its own signed agreement.

start.title: How we start
start.body: We start with a short call and write the scope. Work begins once both sides agree on that document.

phases.title: Phasing and staged delivery
phases.body: Work ships in defined phases, each with its own usable output. Payment is tied to those same phases.

revisions.title: Revisions
revisions.body: Each phase includes two revision rounds. Further rounds or a scope change are estimated as a new phase.

clientDuties.title: What we need from you
clientDuties.body: Content and images, access to your current channels, and one person who can make decisions. Delays on these three move the timeline.

ip.title: IP and code ownership
ip.body: Source, domain, hosting, and every key belong to your organization. No part of the system stays locked to us.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality
confidentiality.body: Your business and customer data stay confidential. If you'd rather not be named in our work, the case is published anonymously or not at all.

thirdParty.title: Third-party running costs
thirdParty.body: Servers, domains, AI models, and SMS carry running costs. These are separate from the build fee and the accounts are opened in your name.

support.title: Support scope
support.body: Fixing what we built is free during the warranty period. New features, content changes, and work on other systems are not support and are estimated separately.

stop.title: Stopping or withdrawing
stop.body: Either side can stop between phases. Work completed to that point is settled and handed over; nothing is held hostage.

Repeat.title: How much revenue is sitting in your past customers?
Repeat.subtitle: Use your own numbers to see what automatic reminders bring back each month.

interval.label: How often would they naturally rebuy?

returning.label: What share actually come back today?

multiple.label: Cost to win a new customer vs. bring one back (estimated)

Repeat.disclaimer: This is an estimate from your own inputs, not a sales guarantee. The achievable return rate is deliberately conservative.

full.title: Repeat-customer calculator
full.intro: Your biggest revenue source is someone who already bought. See how much of it is left on the table.
full.methodBody: Recoverable revenue = customers due to rebuy this month × achievable lift in return rate × average purchase.
assumptions: Customers due each month = total customers ÷ rebuy interval.
The achievable lift is held at a conservative 15 percentage points and never pushes the return rate past 100%.
The acquisition-cost ratio is a rounded approximation, not a figure quoted from a specific published source.
